- Model consistently underestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days), suggesting a persistent downward bias.
- Forecasts tend to overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., 70+ → 72+), then correct sharply — model overreacts to recent highs and fails to capture mean reversion.
- Model exhibits lag in responding to true price increases; true price rises often occur before model forecasts catch up.
- Forecasts show a tendency to “smooth” volatility — underestimating sharp upward moves and overestimating downward ones.
- Model performs better in the latter half of the forecast (last 10–15 days) when prices are more stable or trending upward — suggests horizon-dependent accuracy.
- When true price is above 70, model often underestimates the magnitude of the rise, especially if preceded by a spike.
- Model frequently fails to capture the “tail” of a price surge — i.e., the final 3–5 days of a spike are often underestimated.
- Forecasts show a tendency to “climb too fast” in the first few days after a price spike, then plateau — suggesting a failure to model the decay phase after a peak.
